locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (EE+ H-rearrangement not involving the charge site)

evidence.curator_note: First step of eq 4.44 (arrow labelled 'i', inductive cleavage). The 1,3-dichlorobutane molecular ion is drawn n-ionized at the secondary chlorine (Cl carries '+.'): CH3-C(+.)HCl-CH2-CH2Cl. ARC COUNT: the book draws 1 arc - a single full-headed (two-electron) arrow whose tail sits on the C2-Cl1 sigma bond and whose head points at the charged chlorine (Cl1, the '+.'). This is charge-site-driven inductive heterolysis: the C2-Cl1 bonding pair migrates onto Cl1, neutralising it to a chlorine radical (Cl(+.) -> Cl.) and leaving an even-electron secondary carbocation CH3-CH(+)-CH2-CH2Cl (m/z 91). LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge and odd electron are placed on Cl1 in the mapped SMILES ([Cl+] with one sigma bond = Cl(+.), one unpaired electron), matching the '+.' the book draws over that chlorine. ENCODING: the single drawn arc is transcribed exactly as electron_move <1> (bond 1-2 -> atom 1, electron_count 2). The two electrons landing on Cl1 form a new lone pair while its pre-existing odd electron is retained, so the arrow-check reports a soft 'lone pair rather than radicals' note on atom 1 (radical count unchanged at 1); this is expected for a heterolysis onto an already-radical cation site and is not a defect.

locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (EE+ H-rearrangement, 'rH', charge site not involved)

evidence.curator_note: Second step of eq 4.44 (arrow labelled 'rH'): the even-electron secondary carbocation eliminates neutral HCl, giving the resonance-stabilised C4H7(+) cation at m/z 55 (the base peak of 1,3- and 1,1-dichlorobutane per the running text). This is an H rearrangement that does NOT involve the charge site: the departing chlorine (Cl14, on the terminal CH2) abstracts an H from the adjacent CH2 (C8) while the C8=C11 double bond forms and the C11-Cl14 bond breaks. ARC COUNT: the book draws 2 arc(s): arc(1) runs from a chlorine lone pair (drawn as the ':' on Cl14) to the hydrogen on C8 (Cl abstracts H); arc(2) runs from the C8-H sigma bond into the forming C8=C11 pi bond. The book does NOT draw the C11-Cl14 heterolysis - the departure of chlorine as part of HCl is left IMPLICIT (Cl14 is simply written into the HCl product). For full electron balance an implicit third hook, C11-Cl14 sigma -> Cl14 lone pair, is required (not drawn on the page). ENCODING NOTE: because RDKit strips atom-mapped hydrogens in this build, the two drawn arcs (both terminate on / originate from the migrating H) are not directly transcribable. The heavy-atom skeleton change (form C8=C11, break C11-Cl14) is instead encoded as a single re-decomposed two-electron move <1> = bond 11-14 -> bond 8-11 (the C11-Cl14 sigma pair routed into the new C8=C11 pi bond); the complementary C8-H -> H-Cl14 transfer that supplies chlorine's H is folded into the implicit-H counts (C8: CH2 -> =CH; Cl14: Cl -> HCl). This re-decomposition preserves exactly the drawn heavy-atom transformation; no heavy-atom bond change is omitted, but the encoded move is NOT a verbatim copy of either drawn arc. RESONANCE (convention C): the product is the 1-methylallyl / methallyl cation, drawn here in the localized form CH3-CH(+)-CH=CH2 (charge on C2); its allylic resonance partner CH3-CH=CH-CH2(+) carries the charge on C11 and is the reason for the ion's stability and base-peak intensity. PRINTED INTENSITY: none - the page prints no numeric percentages; the text only states m/z 55 is 'the base peak', a qualitative statement, so relative_intensity is omitted.

Cross-linked to MOD rules IMS_4_44_ind (inductive cleavage) and IMS_4_44_rH (H-rearrangement). VERIFIED bond-by-bond against their DFS. IMS_4_44_ind '[Cl+.]1[C]2([C]3(H3))(H)[C]8(H2)[C]11(H2)[Cl]14 >> [Cl.]1 . [C]3(H3)[C+]2(H)[C]8(H2)[C]11(H2)[Cl..]14' breaks the C2-Cl1 bond, drops both electrons onto Cl1 (Cl(+.) -> .Cl) and leaves C2 as an even-electron carbocation - identical to step_inductive_cleavage (the DFS map 1/2/3/8/11/14 line up 1:1 with this record's maps). IMS_4_44_rH '[C]1(H3)[C+]5(H)[C]7(H2)[C]10(H2)[Cl..]13 >> [C]1(H3)[C+]5(H)[C]7(H){=}[C]10(H2) . [Cl]13[H]' forms the C7=C10 double bond, transfers one H from C7 to Cl13 and expels HCl while the cation stays on C5 - the same net change as step_h_rearrangement (rH-rule maps 1/5/7/10/13 correspond to this record's maps 3/2/8/11/14). In BOTH rules the cleaved bond is incident to the atom(s) that reorganise: for rH the cleaved C10-Cl13 bond is incident to C10, which forms the new C10=C7 pi bond - correct geometry, so neither rule is mis-encoded relative to the book (no mismatch). Charge/radical are localised exactly as the book draws (Cl-ionized molecular ion; even-electron carbocation, then allyl cation). Computed monoisotopic m/z (electron-mass-corrected cations, RDKit ExactMolWt) are curator-derived: precursor 125.9992, m/z 91.0304, m/z 55.0537; the page prints no numeric intensities.
